title: grain/trigger@v1: when an event happens, file work (docs/task-repos.md §6.2). on: names one or more event sources, each with its own options; fires: names what to file. A trigger never holds a merge: that is kind: gate (§6.3). Last and next fire, pause and run history are runtime only

on.description: The event sources, GitHub Actions' on: shape: each key is a source and its value that source's options. Quote the key in front matter: a YAML 1.1 reader takes a bare on for true. task-closed is reserved for a later minor version and refused until then (§6.2)

fires.description: Exactly one of: a template plus inputs, which files a task where the firing's task home says (§5.5); or a workflow run followed by a review task, as a workflow's on.schedule behaves in grain today

template.description: Unpinned, so a firing renders the template's current revision and records it in the task's template.rev

bind.description: Template input name -> event field (event.fired_at, event.to_sha, event.paths, event.group, event.requirement, …). Data, not Jinja: front matter is never rendered

context.description: Entries added after the template's; no input: entries (§5.6)

per.description: design-change only: one task per push (event, the default) or one per changed requirement, by the planning table of §7.4

workflow.description: A .grain/workflows/*.yml file in the trigger's own repo, by plain path (§12.2). Run at the branch the trigger names

branch.description: The branch the workflow runs at; grain's schedule base:. Default: the repo's default_ref

review.description: The review task filed once the run finishes, with its result. Default: grain's built-in workflow-review template

fires_in.description: Who fires it: silo files into the team intake; grain means every Grain whose trigger roots list it fires it into its own root. A workflow run needs a Grain: fires.workflow requires grain

enabled.description: The reviewed on/off switch. Pausing and suspending are runtime, in the database

limits.description: Firings this trigger may make; each can only lower the Grain's or Silo's own caps (§11.36)

derived_from.description: Provenance only: the trigger this one was customised from, which the same Grain ignores in its trigger entry (§6.2). A reference: it activates nothing and inherits nothing

schedule.description: A cadence (exactly one of grain's cadence keys) plus its options

timezone.description: IANA zone; empty or absent is UTC

overlap.description: While the previous firing is unplaced, queued or running: skip this one; file it to wait on the previous (depends_on); or file it and cancel the previous (§8.7). Default skip

catch_up.description: Firings missed while nothing could fire (downtime): none, the latest only, or all, at most max

within.description: Ignore missed firings older than this

change.description: push: any update of a matching branch; merge: a reviewed change landing on one (a merge-queue merge, a merged review branch). Filters as Actions writes them

branches.description: Globs; default the repo's protected refs. Only protected refs may be watched (§11.37)

group_by.description: Split one event into a firing per changed folder or file (grain's {{group}}); default none

debounce.description: Coalesce events this close together into one firing (from_sha of the first, to_sha of the last)

designChange.description: A design object's requirements changing on its default_ref: the planner of §7.4 as an event source

designs.description: Design files or folders (ending in /) to watch

classes.description: Which requirement changes fire; default all three

max_tasks_per_change.description: Above this, one plan proposal is filed instead (§7.4); the design's planning.max_tasks_per_change can lower it

manual.description: An explicit run now, from Silo's UI, the API or the CLI

who.description: Who may request one; default the team's approvers, or the Grain's owner

inputs.description: Template inputs the requester may set; every other input comes from fires.inputs
